## 2017 Toyota Corolla Maintenance Snapshot

The log shows a **steady, low-complexity upkeep pattern** with one larger brake job and mostly routine wear items. At **112,000 km**, the car appears to be maintained on schedule, with service intervals clustering around normal mileage-based needs.

## Cost-Over-Time and Mileage Service Timeline

### Maintenance Log View
| Date | Service | Cost (USD) | Mileage (km) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2024-02-10 | Oil change | 78 | 98,000 |
| 2024-06-15 | Brake pads | 320 | 102,500 |
| 2024-11-03 | Battery | 165 | 107,800 |
| 2025-03-22 | Tire rotation | 60 | 110,400 |
| 2025-05-08 | Air filter | 42 | 111,700 |

### Best Chart Types for the Dashboard
- **Line chart for cost over time**: shows spending spikes and routine maintenance rhythm clearly.
- **Timeline chart or lollipop chart for mileage-based service**: ideal for seeing how services align with odometer progression.
- **Bar chart by service type**: useful for comparing recurring expense categories.
- **Combo chart**: mileage on one axis, cost on the other, if you want one compact executive view.

## Upkeep Pattern Observations

- **Routine maintenance dominates**: oil, tire rotation, and air filter are low-cost items, suggesting normal preventive care rather than major repairs.
- **One clear cost spike**: the **brake pads** service at **$320** is the largest expense and likely the main wear-related event in the period.
- **Service frequency is healthy**: the car received attention roughly every few months, which is a good sign for a vehicle at **112,000 km**.
